q: Can a tea or coffee estate count its shade trees as carbon removals in its footprint?
title: Shade trees as carbon removals on an estate
short: Only the growth in tree carbon can count, not the carbon already standing, and only as removals reported separately from emissions, never netted off. You need repeated tree inventories, a record of trees cut and a plan for reversals, as the GHG Protocol Land Sector and Removals Standard requires.
audience: Tea and coffee estates and their export buyers

p: A mature shade canopy holds a lot of carbon, but it removed that carbon in past years. A removal in your reporting year is the increase in carbon stock over that year: new planting and trees growing larger, minus trees lopped, felled or lost. The IPCC 2006 Guidelines (Volume 4, Chapter 5, Cropland) treat perennial woody biomass the same way, by change in stock.

ol: Map the estate and its shade blocks.
Lay sample plots and record each tree's species, diameter at breast height and height.
Convert to biomass with published allometric equations for those species, add roots with a root to shoot ratio, and take carbon as a fraction of dry biomass (IPCC default 0.47).
Repeat the inventory after a few years and divide the stock change by the years in between.
Subtract carbon in loppings and trees taken for fuel or timber.

ul: Report removals as their own line in t CO2, next to gross emissions, not subtracted from them.
Keep monitoring the stored carbon. A later loss, such as clearing a block, is reported as a reversal.
ISO 14067 product footprints also keep removals and biogenic carbon visible as separate items in the study report.
A buyer can count your removals in its Scope 3 only if it can trace its tea or coffee to your land.

p: Use version 1.1 of the Land Sector and Removals Standard, dated 30 June 2026. It made minor edits to version 1.0 from 30 January 2026, and its effective date is 1 January 2027. This version covers agriculture and CO2 removal technologies, not forestry, so confirm your shade blocks are treated as cropland before you report.
Buyers with SBTi FLAG targets may ask for removals data before 2027.

example.title: Illustrative example: 100 ha of shade blocks
lines: Shade tree carbon: 40 t C per ha in the 2020 inventory, 45 t C per ha in 2025
Stock change: (45 minus 40) x 100 = 500 t C over 5 years = 100 t C a year
Removals: 100 x 44/12 = 367 t CO2 a year, reported as a separate line
Made tea from estate leaf: 10,00,000 kg a year, so 0.37 kg CO2 removals per kg, shown beside the emissions figure, not subtracted
example.note: Stock figures are illustrative. If a block was cleared during the period, its loss comes off the stock change first.

senseible: Senseible records the factory's fuel and electricity emissions from bills, the emissions side of the footprint. Tree carbon stock comes from your field inventories and is reported as a separate removals line.
